claim.quote: The combination of this result with searches by the CMS experiment for H $\to\mathrm{b\overline{b}}$ in other production processes yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations and a signal strength of 1.04 $\pm$ 0.20.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 121801 (2018)

name: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

significance.quote: an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations
significance.value: 5.6σ observed (5.5σ expected), combination with H → bb̄ searches in other production processes

summary.plain: CMS reports the observation of the Higgs boson decaying to bottom quarks, which the paper calls the most prevalent decay mode (predicted branching fraction about 58%). The main contribution comes from events where the Higgs boson is produced together with a W or Z boson.
summary.technical: VH production (W or Z boson plus H → bb̄) in 41.3 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data recorded in 2017: combined with previous VH measurements at 7, 8 and 13 TeV, an excess at m_H = 125.09 GeV with a significance of 4.8 standard deviations (4.9 expected for the SM Higgs boson), signal strength 1.01 ± 0.22. Combined with CMS searches for H → bb̄ in other production processes: observed (expected) significance 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations, signal strength 1.04 ± 0.20.

title: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks
why_it_matters: The paper says a precise measurement of the H → bb rate directly probes the Yukawa coupling of the Higgs boson to a down-type quark and provides a necessary test of the hypothesis that the Higgs field is the source of mass generation in the charged fermion sector of the standard model.
